For a writer, there are few greater pains than losing track of time because you're too absorbed in what you're writing. For my money, though, there's one thing worse: looking up from your desk to discover that everyone else has also forgotten what time it is. As bibliotherapist (图书治疗师) Ella Berthoud says, books are not only useful for helping people connect with themselves; it turns out they can also be a helpful reminder of the world outside their own heads. It's a truth as old as time that shared narratives bring people together. But recently many have noted that reading for pleasure is in decline. While reading on-screen is popular among the younger generation, reading on paper is falling out of fashion. Shazia Rafiq, owner of a bookseller in London, believes face-to-face interaction with books has a unique role to play in building a sense of community.
